learningObjective: Trace where the backward signal travels for REINFORCE, Gumbel-Softmax, and straight-through estimation relative to each method's hard or relaxed forward computation.
mediumRationale: A deterministic stacked SVG is the smallest medium that can align each estimator's forward computation with its distinct backward route. Repeated node positions and solid-versus-dashed arrows expose whether the gradient bypasses, follows, or deliberately differs from the sampling path.

mediumComparison.mermaid: Rejected because a flowchart can show connectivity but offers weak control over aligned forward and backward paths, the central comparison in this lesson.
mediumComparison.svg: Selected because three vertically aligned, deterministic computation paths can distinguish solid forward arrows from dashed backward arrows while remaining legible without horizontal scrolling.
mediumComparison.semanticHtml: Rejected because cards or a table would summarize properties but would not make the gradient's route around or through the sampling operation spatially explicit.
mediumComparison.interaction: Rejected because changing temperature could illustrate relaxation sharpness but would distract from the prior concept readers need: which computational path supplies each estimator's gradient.
mediumComparison.paperReuse: Rejected because the primary papers' figures are not needed to explain this general mechanism, and public paper access does not establish figure-reuse permission. No source figure, data, layout, code, or wording is copied.
mediumComparison.noVisual: Rejected because prose and equations describe each estimator independently but require the reader to mentally overlay forward and backward computation to understand why their bias, variance, and differentiability requirements differ.

pages.insight: Introduces gradients of expectations with stochastic or non-differentiable functions, then motivates REINFORCE for sampled discrete actions and delayed rewards.
Derives the score-function identity, states that its Monte Carlo estimate is unbiased and noisy, and explains that control variates reduce its high variance.
Explains pathwise gradients for continuous reparameterizable variables and why their variance generally behaves better, providing the immediate contrast for discrete relaxations.

Directly covers Gumbel-Softmax as a continuous relaxation with temperature-controlled bias and variance, and identifies pretending the stochastic variable is the identity on the backward pass as straight-through estimation.
Extends the sequence to control-variate estimators REBAR and RELAX, confirming that REINFORCE and Concrete pathwise gradients can be combined rather than representing unrelated problem settings.

deckReview.notes: All 214 pages of the local PDF were text-searched for gradient estimator, REINFORCE, score function, categorical, discrete, Gumbel, Concrete, and straight-through terminology. The full relevant run on pages 51-55 was extracted and inspected along with neighboring pages 50 and 56. Page 50 concludes normalization and page 56 begins neural-network project guidance, so neither adds estimator content. The visual preserves the sequence's forward-versus-backward distinction but does not reproduce any slide image, code, wording, or layout.

sources.title: Simple statistical gradient-following algorithms for connectionist reinforcement learning
sources.usage: Used as the primary REINFORCE source to verify the sampled-reward-weighted log-probability gradient and its unbiased stochastic-gradient interpretation.
sources.license: The publisher record is authoritative, but no open figure-reuse license was established. No text, equation rendering, figure, data, or layout is copied; only the mathematical mechanism informs an original diagram.

sources.title: Categorical Reparameterization with Gumbel-Softmax
sources.usage: Used as a primary source to verify the differentiable categorical relaxation, temperature behavior, and pathwise optimization through a soft sample.
sources.license: The arXiv record permits public distribution of the paper but is not treated as general permission to reuse figures. No paper figure, result, wording, data, or layout is reproduced.

sources.title: The Concrete Distribution: A Continuous Relaxation of Discrete Random Variables
sources.usage: Used as the independent concurrent primary formulation to verify that replacing discrete variables with Concrete relaxations enables automatic differentiation while optimizing a biased relaxed objective.
sources.license: Public arXiv availability is not treated as figure-reuse permission. The implementation is an original computation-path comparison and copies no figure, code, prose, data, or layout.

sources.title: Estimating or Propagating Gradients Through Stochastic Neurons for Conditional Computation
sources.usage: Used as a primary source to verify the straight-through heuristic: copy the gradient with respect to a stochastic neuron's output directly as an estimator for the gradient with respect to its input.
sources.license: No general figure-reuse permission was established from the arXiv record. No source figure, prose, experiment, or layout is reused.

sources.title: Gradient Estimation Using Stochastic Computation Graphs
sources.usage: Used to cross-check the computation-graph distinction between score-function terms for stochastic nodes and pathwise backpropagation through differentiable deterministic dependencies.
sources.license: No source artifact is copied and no figure license is relied upon; the paper's formal gradient decomposition is cited only to validate the original visual's paths.

sourceReview.notes: The hardest mental model in the complete article is not the estimators' property table but the mismatch between what happens in the forward pass and where a usable derivative comes from. The original visual therefore uses no empirical values or paper-specific geometry. Solid and dashed routes, arrow direction, explicit hard/soft labels, and text annotations encode every distinction independently of color.

agentReview.summary: Read the full article, searched all 214 source-deck pages and inspected the complete pages 50-56 neighborhood, then checked four primary estimator papers and the stochastic-computation-graph formalism before selecting an original forward-versus-backward path comparison.

implementation.accessibility: The SVG has a linked title and detailed description that states every forward and backward route. Solid right-pointing arrows always encode forward computation; dashed left-pointing arrows always encode backward signals, while hard/soft and forward-only/backward-only labels preserve the lesson without color. The single 360-unit viewBox scales fluidly with no minimum width or horizontal scroll at 390 CSS pixels. Established theme variables provide dark-mode contrast, and the shared print palette forces a light high-contrast canvas and keeps the figure together.
